name: forge
description: Forge in VS Code: an agentic coding assistant wearing the Pajamas design system, extended with Hermes agents and custom endpoints.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Forge runs the Claude Code CLI in the open folder, which loads that folder's .claude settings, hooks and MCP servers. Trust the folder to use Forge.

forge.environmentVariables.description: Environment variables to set when launching Forge

forge.allowDangerouslySkipPermissions.description: Allow bypass permissions mode. Recommended only for sandboxes with no internet access.

forge.cliArgs.markdownDescription:
Extra flags passed straight through to the `claude` CLI that backs Forge.

Keys are flag names with or without leading dashes; values are:
- a string for `--flag value`
- `true` or `null` for a valueless `--flag`
- `false` to switch off a flag Forge sets by default (e.g. `debug`)

Example:
```json
{ "add-dir": "../shared", "allowedTools": "Read,Grep", "mcp-config": "./mcp.json" }
```

Flags the SDK stream protocol depends on (`--print`, `--output-format`, `--input-format`, `--include-partial-messages`, `--permission-prompt-tool`) are rejected, and so are `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions` and `--dangerously-skip-permissions`: bypass is `#forge.allowDangerouslySkipPermissions#` alone. Every other flag is applied. A flag the SDK also derives from an option Forge sets on that launch (for example `--model`, `--permission-mode`, `--setting-sources`, `--thinking`), or one that replaces Forge's own `--debug` or `--settings`, is logged as a duplicate. See the Forge output channel for exactly what was passed.

forge.runDoctorOnStartup.description: Run `claude doctor` when Forge activates and report the CLI version and health in the output channel. Useful because CLI flags drift between versions.

forge.enableNewConversationShortcut.description: Enable Ctrl+N / Cmd+N to start a new Forge conversation while Forge has focus. Off by default because it shadows the editor New File shortcut.

enumDescriptions: Show Forge in the secondary side bar (the right-hand panel).
Show Forge in the primary side bar, from the activity bar.
forge.preferredLocation.markdownDescription:
Where the Forge chat view lives.

`secondary` matches Claude Code: the chat sits in the right-hand panel and the activity bar button opens **Past Conversations**. Forge falls back to the primary side bar on its own when the VS Code build is too old to host a container in the secondary side bar, so you only need `primary` if you prefer the chat on the left, and there the activity bar button opens the chat instead of your history.

forge.showSessionsSidebar.markdownDescription: Show past conversations in their own activity bar container. Claude Code always does; turning this off leaves Forge with no activity bar entry when the chat is in the secondary side bar.

forge.endpointProfile.markdownDescription:
Name of the endpoint profile Forge routes through, from `#forge.endpoints#` or from the profiles directory.

Empty means talk to the Anthropic API directly, with no relay and no behaviour change. Pick one interactively with **Forge: Select Endpoint Profile**.

forge.activeAgent.markdownDescription: The Hermes agent Forge runs as: its persona, model and tool scope. Empty for none. Set by **Forge: Select Agent**; the agent is read from `#forge.agentsDir#`. Applies from the next conversation.

forge.agentsDir.markdownDescription: Folder of Hermes agent files. A relative path is resolved against the first workspace folder. Defaults to `.forge/agents` in the workspace.

forge.agentEndpoints.markdownDescription: Binds an agent to one of your endpoints: agent name to `#forge.endpoints#` profile name. Kept here rather than in the agent file, so sharing an agent does not share one machine's gateway.

forge.endpointProfilesDir.markdownDescription:
Directory of YAML endpoint profiles, a secondary source alongside `#forge.endpoints#`.

Defaults to `~/.forge/endpoints`. A profile defined in both places uses the `#forge.endpoints#` one, and the collision is logged to the Forge output channel.

forge.endpointHealth.syncIntervalMinutes.markdownDescription:
How often Forge checks that each endpoint's model still answers, in minutes. `0` turns the schedule off and leaves it to the refresh button in the model picker and the **Sync** buttons in **Settings → Endpoints**.

**This costs tokens, a few.** Being listed by a gateway is not the same as being servable, so the only reliable check is a real request. Forge sends the smallest one it can, four tokens with no streaming, to the one model each endpoint runs: at the default of 5 minutes that is twelve tiny requests an hour per endpoint. On a metered endpoint, raise this or set it to `0`.

The model picker lists only the endpoints whose model answered, each with its ping; one that did not answer is shown, greyed with the reason, only while it is the one in use. What answered is remembered per machine and never synced: a verdict is a statement about what *this* machine can reach.

description.description: Shown beside the name in the endpoint picker.

enumDescriptions: OpenAI /chat/completions. Forge translates the CLI's Anthropic requests to and from this shape.
Anthropic /v1/messages. Forwarded as-is; no translation.
Neither: supply a transform module that reshapes the request and response yourself.
wire.markdownDescription: The request shape this endpoint speaks. `raw` additionally requires `transform`.

baseUrl.markdownDescription: Origin of the endpoint, with or without a trailing `/v1`.

model.description: The model id this endpoint expects, exactly as it wants it written.

chatPath.markdownDescription: Path appended to `baseUrl`, for gateways that prefix everything. Defaults to `/messages` on the anthropic wire and `/chat/completions` otherwise.

headers.description: Extra headers merged into every request.

query.markdownDescription: Query parameters merged into the request URL, e.g. Azure's `api-version`.

auth.description: How to authenticate. Supply secrets by reference, never by value.

enumDescriptions: No credential.
Authorization: Bearer <value>.
A static credential in the header named by `header`.
OAuth2 client-credentials: fetch a token first, then attach it.
Run a command that prints a token on stdout.

value.markdownDescription:
The credential, for `bearer` and `header`.

**Do not paste the secret itself.** Use `${env:VAR}`, `${file:/path}` or `${secret:KEY}` (VS Code SecretStorage), resolved at request time.

exchange.description: Token request run before the model request, for kind: exchange.

body.markdownDescription: Form or JSON body. Interpolates `${env:...}` and `${secret:...}`.

tokenPath.description: Dot-path into the JSON response holding the token, e.g. access_token.

expiresInPath.description: Dot-path holding seconds-until-expiry. Falls back to ttlSeconds.

attachAs.description: How the resulting token rides on the model request.

exec.description: Command printing a token to stdout, for kind: exec.

ttlSeconds.description: How long the printed token is cached before the command runs again.

tls.description: Client certificates and trust, for endpoints behind corporate TLS.

caBundle.markdownDescription: Extra CA bundle(s): a path, a list of paths, or `"system"` to pull the OS trust store.

cert.markdownDescription: Client certificate path, for mTLS. Requires `key`.

pfx.description: PKCS#12 bundle path, as an alternative to cert + key.

insecureSkipVerify.description: Skip certificate verification. An explicit opt-in for a known-broken lab endpoint; it disables the protection that makes the client certificate worth carrying.

servername.description: SNI server name, when it differs from the host in baseUrl.

proxy.description: Proxy to reach the endpoint through.

capabilities.markdownDescription: What this endpoint can actually do. Forge gates its UI on these: a feature declared off has its rows hidden rather than shown and broken. **Forge: Detect Endpoint Capabilities** probes a live endpoint and proposes a block for you to accept.

streaming.description: The endpoint can stream tokens as server-sent events.

tools.description: The model can call tools. Off makes Forge a chat window: no file edits, no commands.

toolChoice.description: The endpoint honours tool_choice, so a tool can be forced.

enumDescriptions: A leading message with role: system.
A top-level system field beside messages.
No system role: prepend the text to the first user message.

contextWindow.markdownDescription: Total context in tokens. Drives auto-compaction and how aggressively large tool output is filtered before the model sees it: a 32k model needs far more filtering than a 200k one, so getting this right matters more than it looks.

enumDescriptions: Trust the usage field the endpoint returns.
Estimate locally. Safe when the endpoint reports nothing or reports zeros.
tokenCounting.markdownDescription: How to count context fill. Compaction fires off these numbers, so an endpoint that returns zeroed `usage` must use `heuristic` or long sessions will run into a context-overflow error instead of compacting.

maxImageBytes.description: How much base64 image data one request may carry. A body budget, not a token budget: gateways with a body cap answer an oversized POST with a 413. Oldest images are dropped first; the newest is always sent.

parallelToolCalls.description: The model can ask for several tool calls in one turn.

enumDescriptions: Emit Anthropic cache_control breakpoints.
Send nothing, but keep the prompt prefix byte-stable so a vLLM or SGLang prefix cache hits.
Neither.
promptCaching.markdownDescription: How the stable head of the prompt is cached, for latency. `prefix` is the useful setting for most self-hosted servers.

parallelToolExecution.description: Run requested tools concurrently when none of them can mutate the workspace.

effort.markdownDescription:
This endpoint honours a reasoning-effort knob. Gates the effort rows in the composer.

The CLI's effort ladder is client-side, so it keeps *working* against any endpoint; this declares whether it keeps *meaning* anything. A gateway that silently drops the field would otherwise offer four rungs that all produce the same answer.

effortLevels.markdownDescription: Which effort values this endpoint honours. Ultracode is offered only when `xhigh` is listed.

enumDescriptions: vLLM and DeepSeek-shaped APIs.
OpenRouter and several aggregators.
The endpoint reasons invisibly, or not at all.
reasoningField.description: Which streamed delta field carries reasoning text, so Forge can re-emit it as a thinking block.

fastMode.description: There is a faster cut of this model worth exposing as "Toggle fast mode".

fim.description: The endpoint can fill in the middle fast enough for inline ghost-text completion.

image.description: Image generation, when this endpoint offers it. Omit the block and Forge exposes no image tool.

transform.markdownDescription: Path to a JS module exporting `transformRequest` / `transformResponse`, run in a separate V8 context with a 5-second timeout. It is not a security sandbox: only point this at code you trust. Required for `wire: raw`.

http2.markdownDescription: Negotiate HTTP/2 with the origin. **A last resort.** It fixes the stalled non-streaming POST on NVIDIA NIM, but measured against a streaming completion it took the same request from under a second to over five minutes. Raise `timeoutMs` first.

timeoutMs.description: Per-request timeout. A cold-starting self-hosted model may need considerably more than the default.

retries.markdownDescription: Retries for **connection-level** failures only: refused, reset, DNS, TLS. HTTP statuses are passed straight through to the CLI, which does its own 429/529 backoff; retrying them here too would multiply the wait.

extraBody.description: Merged into every request body, for provider-specific knobs.

models.markdownDescription:
Every model this endpoint serves. When present, this replaces the CLI's built-in model table in the Forge picker, since that table lists Anthropic tiers your gateway does not serve, so showing it would offer models that cannot answer.

UI gating is the **intersection** of these entries and `capabilities`: a model claiming `supportsEffort` against an endpoint whose `capabilities.effort` is false stays greyed out. Populate the ids with **Forge: List Endpoint Models**.

id.description: The model id this endpoint expects, exactly as it wants it written.

displayName.description: Shown in the model picker. Defaults to the id.

supportsEffort.markdownDescription: This model honours a reasoning-effort knob. Intersected with `capabilities.effort`; defaults to it when omitted.

supportedEffortLevels.markdownDescription: Effort rungs for this model. Intersected with `capabilities.effortLevels`. Ultracode is offered only when `xhigh` survives that intersection.

contextWindow.markdownDescription: Per-model context window. Falls back to `capabilities.contextWindow`.

unavailable.description: Show the model greyed out rather than selectable, as the official picker does for models an account cannot use.

modelMap.markdownDescription:
Rewrites model ids on the way out, keyed by the id the CLI sends.

The CLI makes internal small-model calls (conversation titles, memory, subagent chores) using ids from its own table, which your gateway will not recognise. Run a session, then check the Forge output channel: every distinct id the relay sees is logged, so you can map exactly the ones that appear instead of guessing.
